title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` and a list of range queries, for each query `[left, right]` compute the sum of the elements of `nums` between indices `left` and `right` inclusive. Since `nums` never changes between queries, precompute whatever you need once so that each individual query can be answered quickly. Implement this as a function `range_sum_queries(nums, queries)` that returns a list of the answers, one per query, in order.
hints: Recomputing the sum of a range from scratch for every query is O(n) per query — with many queries that adds up fast.
Precompute a prefix sum array once: prefix[i] = sum of nums[0..i-1]. Then any range sum is a difference of two prefix values.
sum(nums[left..right]) = prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left]. This turns each query into O(1) work after an O(n) one-time setup.

solution.approach: Build a prefix sum array once where prefix[i] holds the sum of the first i elements of nums (prefix[0] = 0). Any inclusive range sum from left to right can then be computed as prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left], since that subtracts off everything before left while keeping everything through right. This turns what would be O(n) work per query into O(1) per query after a single O(n) precomputation, which is the entire point of treating this as a DP-style prefix computation over an immutable array.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n + q) where q is the number of queries
